title: A rank test found no clear rise in dry-spell flow decline at 282 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We test whether a reported dry-spell decline rise survives removal of any fixed increasing map of daily flow within each era. We define a leave-one-out rank fall and prove exact finite-sample invariance to such maps. In the planned CAMELS-AUS v2.03 test at 282 south-east Australian catchments, 2010-2021 versus 1951-1996, rank fall changed by -0.00690. Joint five-year block and spatial 95% limits were -0.02069 to +0.01905. A later test of the published matching rule reproduces its normalized decline rise: +0.02177 [0.00497, 0.04289] at 285 catchments. The rank contrast on those same events is +0.00366 [-0.00459, 0.03118]. A full matching grid shows that zero-start eligibility matters more for the decline index than the bin choice. An exact log-normal example shows that rank fall depends on recession rate divided by the spread of log starting flow. Thus a null rank test cannot prove an unchanged physical clock. This study supplies a method and limits on interpretation, not a cause of the annual runoff loss. Coarse weather matching, zero-flow ties, changing support and a short test era limit inference. All plans, follow-up decisions, code, proofs, source hashes, aggregate results, draws, audits and figures are included.
